# AAN Corpus Sweep Findings

> **Generated sweep report** — produced by an automated adversarial consistency sweep of the Federal Application-Aware Networking corpus. Scope: **68 series books, 30 training-program pages, 45 deck/spec YAMLs, and 2 deployable ServiceNow kits**, reviewed against in-repo SSOTs (`orgcomp-compliance-spine.yml`, `orgcomp-authority-deadlines.yml`, `reference/nist-800-53r5-controls.json` v5.2.0, `OrgComp_CR26_Reconciliation.md`, `OrgComp_Evidence_Contract_Spec.md`, shipped code artifacts). All HIGH findings were **dual-adversarially verified** (independently re-derived from the cited SSOT before confirmation); MED findings that failed dual confirmation were demoted and are marked as such. The input finding stream was truncated mid-record on the final MED entry (Vol III Book 06, line 109); counts below reflect the findings as received.

## 1. Executive Summary

| Severity | Count | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **HIGH (confirmed)** | **113** | Every HIGH survived dual-adversarial verification |

### Five most consequential findings

1. **The "29 CR26 KSIs" conflation is systemic** (Vol 0 Book 00:1181; Vol IV Book 06:216; Vol IV Book 05:69; Vol V Books 00/01; training `compliance-track.qmd`, `index.qmd`, `book-19.qmd`; specs `Vol_IV_Book_05.yaml`). At least ten files assert full CR26 coverage that the corpus's own reconciliation SSOT (`OrgComp_CR26_Reconciliation.md`: 46 indicators, 19 mapped) explicitly disclaims. A hostile ISSO reading any one of these files takes it as a claim of full CR26 catalog coverage — the single highest-blast-radius credibility defect in the corpus.
2. **Vol IV Book 06 Appendix A fabricates CR26 indicator IDs** (`Vol_IV_Book_06_OrgComp_Authorization_Package_ConMon.qmd:713`). 17 of 29 rows carry indicator IDs (KSI-MLA-MAU/ESH/DLP, KSI-INR-IRR/MLE/NTA, KSI-RPL-BCP/BCT/DRP/DRT, etc.) that do not exist in the 46-indicator CR26 list — in the authorization package book itself.
3. **The compliance app's safety invariants do not hold in production** (`x_ssa_fed_compliance/script-includes/ComplianceGate.js:36` and `:57`). `verify()` fails open — a dead tenant connection closes tasks with passing CA-7 evidence — and the write-scope refusal the app's attestation argument rests on is a stub that returns `false` unconditionally outside test mode, with ATF tests providing false assurance.
4. **Unvalidated dynamic dispatch in the day-2 flow is a privilege-escalation surface** (`servicenow-day2/flow/flow-blueprint.md:49`). `c[inputs.action](...)` with no allowlist lets a crafted flow input invoke arbitrary Microsoft Graph calls under the app credential, bypassing every per-action control mapping.
5. **BOD 22-01 misattribution propagates through the vulnerability-management lane** (Vol III Book 02:74; training `book-11.qmd:29`; `labs/lab-b6-sentinel.qmd:73`). The 14/28-day internet-facing/internal split is not BOD 22-01 (which keys on per-entry KEV `dueDate`); it is the BOD 26-04 model per the deadline SSOT — and the lab script downloads the KEV catalog, then ignores the `dueDate` field it just parsed. Runner-up: the Vol II Book 02 NTLM discovery script (`:229`) filters on the wrong event property and always returns empty — fabricated-clean closure evidence.

## 2. Confirmed HIGH Findings

### Vol 0 — Keystone documents

#### H-001 — `Vol_0_Book_00_OrgComp_Executive_Summary.qmd:745` — count-not-reproducible
- **Claim:** Vol I Book 01 closes 16 NIST controls (lines 712, 718, 745; repeated in the Control Count Comparison table at 1089).
- **Problem:** The "16" is immediately followed by an 18-item enumeration (22 distinct control IDs; 17 distinct base controls under the series' own folding convention). No counting convention yields 16; the table above it has 18 rows.
- **Fix:** Recount under one stated convention (17 base / 18 rows / 22 IDs) and update every occurrence of "16", including the es-fig-01 alt text and summary tables.

- **Fix:** Recount (13 rows / 15 base) and propagate to the heading, summary table, and es-fig-01 alt text.

### Vol I

#### H-010 — `Vol_I_Book_01_OrgComp_Cloud_Landing_Zone_IPAM_FedRAMP.qmd:281` — scope-violation
- **Claim:** "SSA inherits both the InfoBlox CSO (FR2017257053) and the AWS GovCloud infrastructure authorization — layered FedRAMP coverage" (High cited).
- **Problem:** An agency consuming a SaaS CSO does not separately inherit the underlying IaaS authorization; AWS GovCloud is a leveraged authorization inside InfoBlox's package and its High baseline confers nothing to SSA's Moderate boundary. Shared-responsibility misstatement a 3PAO rejects.
- **Fix:** Under Path A SSA inherits only from the InfoBlox CSO at Moderate; note InfoBlox leverages AWS GovCloud within its own package — no second inheritance.

### Vol IV

#### H-043 — `Vol_IV_Book_01_OrgComp_Business_Continuity.qmd:119` — factual-misattribution
- **Claim:** "NIST SP 800-34 Rev 1 defines seven sections for a federal Contingency Plan" (also lines 42, 699).

### Deployable kits (ServiceNow)

#### H-099 — `servicenow-day2/script-includes/EntraHelpdeskGate.js:41` — fail-open
- **Claim:** Header: the gate "re-reads the target through Graph and confirms the intended state actually took — closure proven by observation".
- **Problem:** `verify()` only GETs `/users/{userId}` and returns ok on any 2xx — it never compares returned state to intended state, and for group/license/guest actions it reads the wrong object entirely. A failed disable passes verify and gets stamped as CM-3/AU-2 evidence — the exact failure mode the header claims to prevent.
- **Fix:** Make verify() action-aware: fetch the relevant object, assert the expected property, return ok=false with observed-vs-expected delta on mismatch.

#### H-100 — `servicenow-day2/flow/flow-blueprint.md:49` — least-privilege
- **Claim:** Step 4: `var r = c[inputs.action](inputs.target_id, inputs.opts);`.
- **Problem:** Unvalidated dynamic dispatch on flow input. `inputs.action = '_graph'` invokes the internal method with attacker-chosen HTTP verb and path — arbitrary Graph calls under the app credential, bypassing every per-action mapping. `initialize`/`type` also reachable.
- **Fix:** Dispatch through an explicit allowlist keyed by the catalog item's control_key; never index the client object with raw input.

#### H-101 — `x_ssa_fed_compliance/script-includes/ComplianceGate.js:36` — fail-open
- **Claim:** `verify()` implements closure-by-observation ("re-reads the same surface, confirms the drift is gone").
- **Problem:** Closure is inferred from **absence**, and a failed re-read looks like success: a READ_FAILED sentinel's asset never matches `task.asset`, so verify returns `{closed:true}` with RETEST_PASSED. A dead tenant connection closes the task with passing CA-7 evidence. Same fail-open for wrong `task.surface` (anything non-'azure' silently re-reads M365), paging, deleted resources.
- **Fix:** Fail closed: treat any READ_FAILED sentinel as retest-inconclusive; require affirmative observation of `task.asset` in a successful read; validate `task.surface` explicitly.

#### H-102 — `x_ssa_fed_compliance/script-includes/ComplianceGate.js:57` — least-privilege / unsupported-claim
- **Claim:** "if the identity is detected holding write scopes... the gate refuses to run at all" (header 13–15; rest/README.md 17–19) — stated as shipped structural fact.
- **Problem:** `_identityHoldsWrite()` returns false unconditionally in production; the refusal exists only under test_mode via a fixture. The ATF test passes against the fixture while the production path is a no-op — false assurance on the invariant the app's central attestation argument rests on.
- **Fix:** Implement the Graph appRoleAssignments/oauth2PermissionGrants read and refuse on `*.ReadWrite.*`, or make the unimplemented state fail closed; reword header and README to per-tenant required completion.

#### H-103 — `x_ssa_fed_compliance/script-includes/ComplianceIngest.js:21` — js-cannot-run-on-servicenow
- **Claim:** ATF suite "runnable via x_ssa_fed_compliance.test_mode = true"; three Script Includes importable in scope.
- **Problem:** All three call `new GSLog(...)` in initialize() (ComplianceIngest.js:21, ComplianceReconcile.js:16, ComplianceGate.js:22). GSLog is a **global** Script Include; from a scoped app it must be `new global.GSLog(...)`. As written, initialize() throws, no class instantiates, and none of the seven ATF tests can execute — including in test_mode.
- **Fix:** `new global.GSLog(...)` or gs.info/gs.warn/gs.error scoped logging.

## 6. Closing Note — Gate Rules vs One-Time Fixes

### Should become new gate rules (recurrence-proven classes)

1. **Control-title verification against `reference/nist-800-53r5-controls.json`** for any `| <CTRL-ID> | <Title> |` table row in .qmd/spec files. Would have caught ≥15 findings across nine files (AC-11, AU-2 ×4, SI-3 ×3, RA-5(5), SC-20/22, SI-2(3), PT-1/3/4/6, SC-12(1), CA-7(1) ×2, PM-2, AC-6(2)).
2. **Withdrawn-control gate.** Extend the catalog JSON with a `withdrawn` field and reject closure/satisfaction claims against withdrawn IDs. Caught three times independently (SI-3(1) ×2, SC-20(1) ×2, IA-2(11) — the last also lives in a shipped adapter mapping).
3. **KSI vocabulary lint.** Enforce the 10 CR26 theme ids + 46 indicator ids + 29 internal rule ids as the only permissible KSI tokens. Would have caught KSI-CM (×6 files), KSI-EDR, KSI-AU/SI/IR, KSI-DAT/IDM, "Privacy Inventory", "Backup and Recovery", the fabricated Appendix A indicator IDs, and the four "Alerting" mis-expansions. Prerequisite: add KSI family names to an in-repo reference SSOT (none exists today — that absence is why nothing gated H-042).
4. **"29 CR26" collocation lint.** Forbid "29 CR26 KSIs/rules/indicators" and "all 29 CR26" outside the reconciliation file itself. Ten-plus files carry the conflation; a trivial regex gate ends the class.
5. **Extend `orgcomp-authorities-drift.yml` / `render_authorities_table.py --check` to embedded .qmd copies.** Five books shipped stale embeds that the partial-only gate could not see (Vol IX Bks 01/03, Vol III Bks 03/04, Vol VIII Bk 00).
6. **Deadline-claims gate.** Any sentence binding an obligation to a date should be checkable against `orgcomp-authority-deadlines.yml` event text, not just the date. Three HIGHs (H-006, H-045, H-058) had the right date with the wrong obligation attached — the current date-only check passes them.
7. **Hardcoded book-count lint.** Forbid "N-part", "final book", "six books", "nineteenth" style counts in prose (spine header already mandates this pending Phase G). Caught in Vol I Bk 04, Vol IV Bk 06, Vol VII Bk 00, decks.
8. **High-claim gate pattern fix.** The gate missed "Moderate or High" (`Vol_III_Book_01:249`) and unbaselined GCC-High claims (`Vol_IV_Book_02:357`); widen the pattern and re-baseline.

### One-time fixes (no gate value)

Math/unit errors (Vol II Book 03 miles-vs-km cluster), script bugs (4624 property index, PowerShell parse errors, kev_check dueDate, lab-b1 split-horizon, GSLog scoping, ComplianceGate/EntraHelpdeskGate verify logic, flow dispatch allowlist), broken cross-references (VI-01 CA, VI-02 token lifetime, VI-08 FP ramp, training source URLs — though a **link-exists check on training Source URLs** is a cheap sub-gate worth adding), misquoted control text, stale derived numbers in specs (better served by actually regenerating decks from sources than by a new gate), and the individual internal contradictions (M-20-04 clock, DROP LOGIN paragraph, SQL lifecycle conflation, PMO footer).

### Sequencing note

Fix the SSOT-adjacent items first — the crosswalk 146→149 (H-007/H-008/H-009), the Vol V slot taxonomy (H-065), and the CM-8 necessity-anchor location (H-075) — because each is a doc-vs-spine disagreement where the owner must decide which side is intended before dependent fixes (spec regens, deck counts, training pages) can land without churn.
